content: Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, or loss of appetite may occur as side effects of this medication. Pain, irritation, or redness at the injection site is also possible. It is important to remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but can occur. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using streptomycin injection, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other aminoglycoside antibiotics (such as tobramycin or gentamicin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Streptomycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG or typhoid vaccine. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using streptomycin, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has directed you to take low doses of aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams a day), you should continue to take the aspirin as directed. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney function, hearing tests, and streptomycin levels) should be performed regularly. Be sure to keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, it is important to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. Store unmixed medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
